items.title: CNBC Daily Open: Chipping away at the AI boom - CNBC
items.summary: # CNBC Daily Open: Chipping away at the AI boom. * Heavy selling across Asia's biggest tech firms shows more jitters around the AI trade. * Nvidia shares sink on OpenAI funding report, allowing Apple to regain the crown of the world's most valuable company. * Oil prices continue to decline as de-escalation hopes are raised between the U.S. and Iran. *The Nasdaq-South Korea feedback loop continues to link the AI trade from one side of the globe to the other, and today it's to the downside.*. Over the course of Monday, more regions across both France and Spain were evacuated, as firefighters fought to keep the fires away from major cities.

items.title: Stock market today: Nasdaq pares losses as chip stocks sell off, S&P 500 and Dow rise - Yahoo! Finance Canada
items.summary: # Stock market today: Nasdaq pares losses as chip stocks sell off, S&P 500 and Dow rise. US tech stocks diverged on Tuesday as a sell-off in chip stocks underscored concerns about AI circular financing deals, countering a drop in oil prices and earnings optimism. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) pared losses to fall 0.1%. The S&P 500 (^GSPC) rose 0.3%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) added 1% as investors weighed the latest quarterly results. Sentiment on the AI trade has soured amid reports that Nvidia (NVDA) is exploring a $250 billion funding backstop for OpenAI (OPAI.PVT), further intertwining the two companies and heightening worries about circular financing. The Federal Reserve kicks off its two-day policy meeting on Tuesday, and it's one of the hardest policy decisions for the market to call in years. US consumer confidence ticked lower in July to 90.8, according to the Conference Board, as perceptions of the labor market softened.

Nvidia (NVDA, Financials), the semiconductor company best known for artificial intelligence chips, fell 5% Monday as investors questioned the funding structure behind the AI infrastructure boom. GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Signs with NVDA. The decline followed a report that Nvidia was discussing about $250 billion in financing guarantees for an OpenAI data center. Separate talks reportedly involved financing up to $350 billion in OpenAI chip purchases. China's progress in chip equipment and the strong market debut of memory producer CXMT added to fears that established semiconductor leaders could face tougher competition. The market reaction comes before earnings from Apple, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon, which could offer clearer signals on future AI infrastructure spending.
